title: When the Current Burns
premise: Orsen Nystrom, a disgraced mountain guide living off the grid in the northern highlands, is coerced by a desperate survey officer into retracing the route of a vanished government team. The only clue is a journal that ends mid-sentence beside a river that official maps refuse to name. As Orsen follows the current upstream, she uncovers a hidden settlement of people who erased themselves the way she once tried to—including the man whose betrayal got her blacklisted twelve years ago. When the river's source proves to be a geothermal vent about to rupture and flood the valley below, Orsen must choose between exposing the settlement to save thousands downstream or honoring the secrecy she once craved for herself; she chooses the valley, burns her own blacklist file in the process, and finally stops measuring life in miles.
about_author: Sable Dunmore is the pen name of a former wilderness rescue coordinator who spent a decade mapping remote waterways before turning to fiction. She writes adventure novels from a cabin with no road access, which she insists is for research purposes only.

chapters.title: Twelve Years of Miles
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. She guides a wealthy client through a storm on the Kestrel Range, revealing her encyclopedic knowledge of terrain she officially isn't allowed to enter. A checkpoint guard recognizes her name and lets her pass with a warning. Emotional beat: competence masking exhaustion; she counts miles because years have failed her.

chapters.title: The Officer Who Wouldn't Leave
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Survey officer Dagny Holt arrives at Orsen's cabin with news: a six-person government team vanished near the headwaters, leaving gear intact and no tracks. Dagny has Orsen's old blacklist file and offers expungement in exchange for tracking them. Emotional beat: cornered resentment—Orsen refuses, then finds Dagny's evidence too precise to dismiss.

chapters.title: Gear With No Grave
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. At the abandoned campsite, everything is orderly: tents pitched, food cached, boots lined up—as if the team walked away barefoot into snow. The team leader's journal ends mid-word. Emotional beat: professional dread; Orsen has seen people die in mountains, never seen them choose to leave.

chapters.title: The River That Isn't on Maps
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV, with an interlude from the missing team leader's journal. Official charts show the tributary ending at a glacier; Orsen's own memory says otherwise. She decides to follow it upstream alone, telling Dagny nothing. Emotional beat: the pull of the unnamed—the river mirrors the life she erased.

chapters.title: Dagny Follows
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Dagny catches up on the trail, admitting the government suspects the team defected and wants it buried quietly. Their first real argument reveals Dagny's career depends on this mission. Emotional beat: reluctant alliance; two women who both measure worth in duty.

chapters.title: Cold Water, Old Wounds
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. A river crossing nearly kills Dagny; Orsen saves her and confesses a fragment of her past—a rescue gone wrong, a client lost, a scapegoating she never fought. Emotional beat: trust kindled in whitewater; Orsen realizes she hasn't spoken her story aloud in twelve years.

chapters.title: Smoke Where Nothing Should Burn
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Above the tree line they find woodsmoke, cultivated terraces, and a cairn marked with symbols matching the journal's last page. Someone is watching them—footprints appear behind their own. Emotional beat: vertigo of discovery; the forbidden source has inhabitants.

chapters.title: The People Who Erased Themselves
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. They are taken captive and brought to Vaskr, a hidden settlement founded decades ago by people who fled governments, debts, and names. Its elder, Maren, recognizes Orsen's surname. Emotional beat: recognition and terror—these people did deliberately what Orsen stumbled into.

chapters.title: The Man From Mile Zero
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Among Vaskr's residents is Eirik Halvard, the expedition partner whose false testimony blacklisted Orsen twelve years ago—and he is the father of the missing team leader. He begs her help finding his daughter Sela. Emotional beat: fury and grief colliding; the past walks out of the mist wearing a familiar face.

chapters.title: What Sela Found
chapters.summary: Eirik's POV via recovered pages, then Orsen's. Sela's notes reveal the team discovered the vent beneath the source is destabilizing; when she reported it, her superiors ordered silence to protect mining claims downstream. Her team chose exile over complicity. Emotional beat: moral vertigo—duty and truth split down the middle.

chapters.title: Council of Ghosts
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. Vaskr debates: reveal the vent and lose their sanctuary, or stay silent and let the valley towns drown. Eirik argues for disclosure; Maren warns exposure means evacuation and ruin. Emotional beat: a community confronting the cost of its own invisibility.

chapters.title: The Tremor
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. A quake cracks the glacial dam above the vent; meltwater begins pooling behind it. Orsen calculates days, not weeks. Dagny reveals her orders include arresting the defectors. Emotional beat: clock started; every choice now costs someone everything.

chapters.title: Terms of Silence
chapters.summary: Dagny's POV. Torn between orders and what she's witnessed, Dagny secretly radios a partial warning, knowing it will end her career if traced. Orsen catches her and, instead of anger, offers partnership. Emotional beat: love against duty takes root—not romance yet, but loyalty deeper than protocol.

chapters.title: Downstream Logic
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. She plans a descent to warn the valley towns directly, but the only fast route runs through the unstable gorge. Eirik insists on coming; Maren forbids it. Emotional beat: fracture lines—every character choosing whom to betray.

chapters.title: Night Run Through the Gorge
chapters.summary: Orsen and Eirik's POV, alternating. The gorge crossing goes wrong; Eirik saves Orsen at the cost of a shattered leg, repaying twelve years in one act. They speak honestly for the first time about the old betrayal—his cowardice, her silence. Emotional beat: forgiveness as survival, not absolution.

chapters.title: The Valley Refuses to Listen
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. In the lowland town of Brannvik, officials dismiss her warnings—she's a blacklisted guide with no standing. Dagny burns her own career publicly corroborating the claim. Emotional beat: the system's indifference versus individual conviction.

chapters.title: Evacuation in the Rain
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. Brannvik empties under storm skies while Vaskr's residents descend to help, unmasking themselves voluntarily. Maren leads them, choosing her people's dignity over their secrecy. Emotional beat: sacrifice made visible; anonymity traded for action.

chapters.title: The Source Gives Way
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. The glacial dam fails early. Orsen, who knows one remaining high route, goes back up to trigger a controlled diversion channel with charges Dagny requisitioned. Emotional beat: the guide's final test—measuring the mile that matters most.

chapters.title: Where the Current Burns
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV, climax. Alone at the vent, she sets the charges as scalding floodwater rises, redirecting the surge away from the evacuees. Nearly drowned, she is pulled out by Dagny, who refused to leave. Emotional beat: love against duty resolved—Dagny chose her, and Orsen lets herself be chosen.

chapters.title: Afterwater
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. The valley floods fields but loses no lives. Vaskr's existence is public; negotiations begin for amnesty. Dagny faces inquiry; Orsen's testimony—and her burned blacklist file—become the story everyone wants. Emotional beat: exhausted relief; the world remade by one honest current.

chapters.title: Names Given Back
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. At a hearing, Orsen tells the full truth of the original disaster, clearing her record and Eirik's conscience alike. Sela's team is posthumously honored as whistleblowers. Emotional beat: identity reclaimed—names restored, lies retired.

chapters.title: Measuring in Years
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV, closing. Spring: Orsen and Dagny map the new river course together, not for any government but for the valley's future. Orsen plants a cairn at the source bearing Sela's name. Emotional beat: quiet resolution—she measures time now in seasons shared, not miles survived.
